window.JP_SCRIPTS["learning-reflection.html"]={"en": "Welcome to the Reflection. Jonathan began with one practical investigation of sticks and developed two learning pathways: one for fifteen-year-old learners, and one for first-year undergraduates. The project grew through repeated revisions to the teaching materials, activities, navigation, translations and avatar guidance. Those revisions showed that a change to one part could disrupt another, so shared components and checks across languages and devices need to come earlier. Working with AI accelerated drafting and development, but also reinforced the need for human judgement, subject checks and accessibility review. The main lesson is to establish the learners’ needs and agree outcomes with stakeholders before building too much. This is a self-directed prototype based on a fictional brief, not a validated course. The next steps are stakeholder and subject review, keyboard and screen-reader testing, mobile and browser checks, native-speaker review of translations and recordings, and a supervised rehearsal of the practical work. A small pilot should then examine learners’ reasoning, participation and progress against agreed criteria.
